sanskrit: gate rāme praśāntātmā rāmo dāśarathir dhanuḥ varuṇāyāprameyāya dadau haste sasāyakam
english: When that Rāma had departed, the tranquil-souled Rāma Dāśarathi handed the bow together with its arrow into the hand of immeasurable Varuṇa.

sanskrit: abhivādya tato rāmo vasiṣṭha pramukhān ṛṣīn pitaraṃ vihvalaṃ dṛṣṭvā provāca raghunandanaḥ
english: Then Rāma, the joy of the Raghu line, having saluted Vasiṣṭha and the other sages at their head, saw his father overcome with emotion and spoke to him.

sanskrit: jāmadagnyo gato rāmaḥ prayātu caturaṅgiṇī ayodhyābhimukhī senā tvayā nāthena pālitā
english: "Rāma the son of Jamadagni has departed. Let the four-limbed army now march, facing Ayodhyā — that army which has been protected with you as its lord."

sanskrit: rāmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā rājā daśarathaḥ sutam bāhubhyāṃ saṃpariṣvajya mūrdhni cāghrāya rāghavam
english: Hearing Rāma's words, King Daśaratha embraced his son with both arms and inhaled the fragrance of the head of that scion of Raghu.

sanskrit: gato rāma iti śrutvā hṛṣṭaḥ pramudito nṛpaḥ codayām āsa tāṃ senāṃ jagāmāśu tataḥ purīm
english: Hearing that that Rāma had gone, the king, thrilled and overjoyed, set the army in motion and quickly departed thence for the city.

sanskrit: patākādhvajinīṃ ramyāṃ tūryodghuṣṭanināditām siktarājapathāṃ ramyāṃ prakīrṇakusumotkarām
english: The city was beautiful with its rows of banners and pennants, resounding with the proclamation of musical instruments, its royal roads sprinkled with water and strewn with heaped flowers —

sanskrit: rājapraveśasumukhaiḥ paurair maṅgalavādibhiḥ saṃpūrṇāṃ prāviśad rājā janaughaiḥ samalaṃkṛtām
english: — adorned with throngs of people, filled with citizens whose faces were bright with joy at the king's entry and with chanters of auspicious words: into this city the king entered.

sanskrit: kausalyā ca sumitrā ca kaikeyī ca sumadhyamā vadhūpratigrahe yuktā yāś cānyā rājayoṣitaḥ
english: Kausalyā, Sumitrā, and the slender-waisted Kaikeyī, together with the other royal ladies, were engaged in welcoming the daughters-in-law.

sanskrit: tataḥ sītāṃ mahābhāgām ūrmilāṃ ca yaśasvinīm kuśadhvajasute cobhe jagṛhur nṛpapatnayaḥ
english: Then the queens received the supremely blessed Sītā, the illustrious Ūrmilā, and both daughters of Kuśadhvaja.

sanskrit: maṅgalālāpanaiś caiva śobhitāḥ kṣaumavāsasaḥ devatāyatanāny āśu sarvās tāḥ pratyapūjayan
english: Adorned with auspicious utterances and robed in silk garments, all those women swiftly worshipped at the shrines of the gods.

sanskrit: abhivādyābhivādyāṃś ca sarvā rājasutās tadā remire muditāḥ sarvā bhartṛbhiḥ sahitā rahaḥ
english: After saluting those who deserved salutation and receiving the salutations of others, all the princes' wives rejoiced, each delighted and in private together with her husband.

sanskrit: kṛtadārāḥ kṛtāstrāś ca sadhanāḥ sasuhṛjjanāḥ śuśrūṣamāṇāḥ pitaraṃ vartayanti nararṣabhāḥ
english: Having taken wives, having mastered weapons, possessed of wealth and friends, those bulls among men passed their days serving their father obediently.

sanskrit: teṣām atiyaśā loke rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ svayambhūr iva bhūtānāṃ babhūva guṇavattaraḥ
english: Among them, Rāma, whose glory surpassed all in the world and whose valour was true, stood foremost in virtues, even as the Self-born Brahmā stands among all beings.

sanskrit: rāmas tu sītayā sārdhaṃ vijahāra bahūn ṛtūn manasvī tadgatas tasyā nityaṃ hṛdi samarpitaḥ
english: And Rāma, that high-minded one, sported with Sītā through many seasons; his thoughts fixed entirely upon her, he was ever surrendered in her heart.

sanskrit: priyā tu sītā rāmasya dārāḥ pitṛkṛtā iti guṇād rūpaguṇāc cāpi prītir bhūyo vyavardhata
english: Sītā was dear to Rāma as "the wife given by my father," and beyond that, his love grew ever greater on account of her virtues and the excellence of her beauty.

sanskrit: tasyāś ca bhartā dviguṇaṃ hṛdaye parivartate antarjātam api vyaktam ākhyāti hṛdayaṃ hṛdā
english: And her husband moved doubly within her heart; even what arose within was made known, for heart speaks to heart.

sanskrit: tasya bhūyo viśeṣeṇa maithilī janakātmajā devatābhiḥ samā rūpe sītā śrīr iva rūpiṇī
english: And all the more conspicuously did Maithilī, the daughter of Janaka — Sītā, who equalled the goddesses in beauty, a very embodiment of Śrī herself — distinguish herself in his eyes.

sanskrit: tayā sa rājarṣisuto 'bhirāmayā sameyivān uttamarājakanyayā atīva rāmaḥ śuśubhe 'tikāmayā vibhuḥ śriyā viṣṇur ivāmareśvaraḥ
english: United with her, that enchanting daughter of the greatest of kings, exceedingly lovely and desired beyond measure, Rāma the all-pervading shone surpassingly — even as Viṣṇu, lord of immortals, shines in the company of Śrī.
